findings.text: The guard reads its two thresholds from the same record it judges: time_bound and rss_bound come from the fragment's own data-time-bound-ratio and data-rss-bound-kb attributes, so loosening the bound inside the fragment lets a `pass` verdict satisfy the assertion. Pinning 0.2 and 51200 from the plan's done-when rather than reading them back from the artifact would make the guard independent of the record it checks.

The guard applies the one-fifth bound to whole-call aggregate time (4.259/10.259 = 0.42) and to the profile's section_attempts_by_plan cumulative time (1.824/6.347 = 0.287), while section 45's pass condition names the decode: `Pass when the head's decode costs at most a fifth of the base's per call`. The fragment's own profile figures put the decode at 0.596 s against 4.445 s, 0.134 of base, and memory 617 MB below base, so the section's stated condition is met on the quantity it names; the recorded pass-with-limitation and this guard therefore encode a stricter reading than the done-when, and would refuse a `pass` that measured the decode as the plan specifies.
